newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa closes higher, sentiment turns up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa closes higher, sentiment turns up.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended higher on Friday as sentiment turned more optimistic.
July closed up six stg at 1,038 stg per tonne to end on a positive note. Traders said July's close above 1,036 was encouraging.

July also gapped up at the open and hit the highest level since April 29 with help from a large European firm's outright July purchases. Traders estimated the early buying between 700 and 800 contracts.
But July slid in the afternoon when New York opened lower to fill all but one stg of the opening gap, traders noted.
Some traders attributed New York's weakness to speculators and locals' month-end book squaring.
Light, early afternoon origin sales also capped cocoa's gains, traders said.
But the large European firm re-emerged later in the day as a light buyer to pick cocoa up off the floor.

Further optimism for cocoa stemmed from the increase in volume. After lingering in a tight range amid lackluster volume for the past couple of weeks, cocoa's up move coupled with higher turnover was friendly, traders said.
Total volume stood at 6,760 contracts, with July notching 3,173 lots. However, no cocoa options traded again.
Traders expected July to ratchet up to test 1,065, the April 2 high. If July cracks that resistance, traders said a move to 1,100 and possibly, even 1,200 could emerge.
